title: Cohomology of the representable derived restriction comparison
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], its big etale site has all objects and arrows of the fibred category in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps. Its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, direct image has value $(h_*N)(z)=\Gamma(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U,N|_{\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U})$; restrictions are induced by base change, and pullback of a module along a stack morphism means precomposition. Higher direct images are computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be representable by algebraic spaces, meaning every scheme $U\to\mathcal Y$ has algebraic-space fibre product $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}U$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $y:V\to\mathcal Y$ be a scheme test object, put $Z=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, and write $p:Z\to\mathcal X$ and $f_V:Z\to V$. For a big etale module sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal X$, let $r_y$ denote precomposition by $y$ followed by restriction to $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and define $r_p$ similarly with the small etale site of the algebraic space $Z$. Use the canonical small-etale module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For every $i\geq0$, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism $r_y(R^if_*F)\simeq R^i(f_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}(r_pF)$. For a flat arrow $b:V\to V^{\prime}$ over $\mathcal Y$ and its induced cartesian arrow $a:Z\to Z^{\prime}$, this identifies $b^*r_{y^{\prime}}(R^if_*F)\to r_y(R^if_*F)$ with the usual degree-$i$ base-change morphism followed by $R^i(f_V)_*$ of the coefficient comparison $a^*r_{p^{\prime}}F\to r_pF$. No quasi-coherence or qcqs hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 075P, lemma-compare-representable-morphism-cohomology, cohomology sheaves of its canonical derived isomorphism. The separate derived-form obligation is lem-sfb-stack-representable-derived-restriction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-representable-derived-restriction] to the given representable $f$ and test scheme $V$. Write $\Theta_y:r_y(Rf_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}(r_pF)$ for its specified derived comparison. Its restriction functors $r_y,r_p$ are exact. For an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, $Rf_*F$ is represented by $f_*I^\bullet$ and $R^if_*F=H^i(f_*I^\bullet)$ by the convention in the statement. The exact-functor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies $H^i(r_y(f_*I^\bullet))$ canonically with $r_yH^i(f_*I^\bullet)$, through cycles and their quotient by boundaries. Thus applying the cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $\Theta_y$ gives the required isomorphism $\theta_y:r_y(R^if_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R^i(f_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}(r_pF)$. Its canonicity follows from the specified $\Theta_y$ and the natural cycle-quotient comparison; no preservation of injectives by $r_p$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 075P, lemma-compare-representable-morphism-cohomology, module case; homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, applied to the cohomology of the canonical comparison.

proof.text: For the flat arrow $b:V\to V^{\prime}$, the induced $a:Z\to Z^{\prime}$ is its base change, so is flat by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The algebraic spaces $Z,Z^{\prime}$ exist by representability. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-etale-ringed-comparison] to $b$ and $a$: their target structure sheaves pulled back to their sources are flat as modules over the inverse-image ring sheaves. In the tensor pullback formula of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], inverse image with transported scalars is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], and tensoring with the source structure sheaf is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Their composite is therefore exact. (For scalar extension the kernels and cokernels are computed in underlying modules, so exactness over the inverse-image ring also gives exactness over the source structure ring.) Consequently termwise $b^*$ and $a^*$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to them yields the canonical identifications $H^i(Lb^*K)=b^*H^i(K)$ and $H^i(La^*L)=a^*H^i(L)$; the termwise functors compute the derived pullbacks because they already invert quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 073C, lemma-flat-morphism-sites; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, proof by composition of inverse image and flat scalar extension; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0735, section-base-change-map, introductory flat-pullback convention.

proof.text: Let $\rho_b:Lb^*r_{y^{\prime}}(Rf_*F)\to r_y(Rf_*F)$ be the restriction arrow, $c_a:a^*r_{p^{\prime}}F\to r_pF$ the coefficient comparison, and $\beta_b$ the derived small-etale base-change arrow. The final clause of [lem-sfb-stack-representable-derived-restriction] states the equality $\Theta_y\circ\rho_b=R(f_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}(c_a)\circ\beta_b\circ Lb^*(\Theta_{y^{\prime}})$, using the flat identifications of step 2. Apply $H^i$ to this equality. Naturality of the cycle-quotient isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies $H^i(\rho_b)$ with the arrow $b^*r_{y^{\prime}}(R^if_*F)\to r_y(R^if_*F)$: on the chosen complex $f_*I^\bullet$ this is precisely its termwise restriction map passed to cycles modulo boundaries. By definition, the usual degree-$i$ flat base-change map is $H^i(\beta_b)$ under these same identifications (the flat-case construction of Tag 0736). Also $H^i(R(f_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}(c_a))=R^i(f_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}(c_a)$. The resulting equality is exactly the claimed composite with the coefficient comparison. Only representability and flatness of this test arrow were used; neither quasi-coherence nor qcqs entered.

from.place: det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Affine PGL quotients with closed orbits and zero-dimensional stabilizers. Supporting affine-quotient step: Finite inertia gives an adequate coarse moduli space. Supporting input to the finite-inertia coarse-space construction: Passage from invariant global power liftings on the affine rank charts to adequate moduli spaces, then etale descent to the glued map. Flat scalar-section comparison needed in the descent of a power lying in the image of a global algebra map; this does not assert adequate-moduli locality. General cohomological input: preservation of locally quasi-coherent modules and flat comparison maps under qcqs stack direct images. Supporting input: Cohomology of the representable derived restriction comparison.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q37-d0731e964 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 cited statements, the parent's uses (steps 1 and 2 of lem-sfb-stack-higher-images-flat-comparison), Stacks 075P (stacks-sheaves.tex:4056) and 0735/0736 (sites-cohomology.tex:2400-2480). The delivery has no new nodes, does not change the statement and does not reopen a re-split. The item is the per-degree H^i consequence of the unsplit same-unit derived node lem-sfb-stack-representable-derived-restriction, which is the layout the brief asks for. There is no cycle. Step 1: H^i of Θ_y, using exactness of r_y from the derived node and the exact-functor Mathlib leaf; it never claims that restriction preserves injectives. Step 2: a is flat as the base change of b (chartwise calculus); O_Z is flat over a^{-1}O_{Z'} (space flat ringed comparison); a^* is the composite of the exact a^{-1} (lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact) and the exact flat tensor (def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules). This is the 04JC proof from cited statements, and termwise pullback computes the derived pullback as in 0735. Step 3: H^i of the derived node's stated canonical equality, with the degree-i base change taken as H^i of the 0736 map. Edge cases checked: i=0, F=0, empty V or X, b=id. No quasi-coherence or qcqs hypothesis is used. Batch 5: chartwise calculus and the flat ringed comparison reach sec-trace-formula only through def-trf-algebraic-space and foundational space models; lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact is a generic topos exactness tool. None of the three is a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, so all are accepted, and the declared tool_use is accepted. No duplicate found: the only 075P nodes are the item, its sibling and the parent, and the flat pullback exactness node is the Zariski analogue. No SGA is cited. proof_deps equals the union of step uses.
